items.rationale: The failed heating-pipe joint and necessary reconnection fall under §§2.4.2–2.4.3 and 7.1.7(c). Allow about €10 each for the first set of four, consistent with Case 40.
A second set of four same-size elbows is not substantiated for the one-metre repair under §7.1.8(c), (e). If separately documented as necessary, four would cost about €40 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers 28 mm fittings only if needed at the reconnection; five are not established by the claim description. If some were needed, allow about €21 each, or €42 for two.
Five additional 28 mm bends are not supported by the documented repair under §7.1.8(e). If one distinct bend is verified as necessary, allow about €22.
A single transition bend is plausible but must correspond to the actual reconnection under §§7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e). Case 40 supports about €22 for one.
Necessary fixings are covered by §7.1.7(c). Case 40 supports about €9 gross for eight screws.
Section 7.1.8(e) requires the clamp size to match the documented work; no 10 mm pipe is documented. If a distinct use is established, Case 43 supports €19 for four.
Matching supports for the repaired 15 mm pipe are allowed under §7.1.7(c). Allow about €20 gross for the four-clamp line.
Necessary plumbing labour is covered at customary rates under §7.1.7(g). At about €91 gross per hour, 6.75 hours comes to €614, consistent with Cases 40 and 43.
The description confirms a helper for part of the repair, and §7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour. At about €67.50 gross per hour, 5.75 hours comes to €388.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) allow the approximately one metre installed, not the unsupported 6.4 m billed. Case 40's €90 for 6.4 m implies about €15 gross for the documented length.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows one travel charge per contractor per invoice. Cases 40 and 43 support about €77 gross for this first charge.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers repair consumables not already itemised, subject to the duplicate-cost exclusion in §7.1.8(c). Allow €35 gross for the flat-rate line, near Case 40.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes processing charges added to itemised labour and materials. The positive figure is nominal only.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like insulation on the repaired section, but §7.1.8(e) excludes unsupported length. Allow €22 gross for about one metre, in line with Case 39.

No separate use for six mats is documented beyond the pipe insulation already billed, so §§7.1.8(c), (e) weigh against payment. If a separate fitting wrap is verified, allow about €18 gross for the necessary material.

Wire used to secure the replacement insulation is a covered fastening under §7.1.7(c). Allow about €12 gross for the quantity attributable to this short repair; the two pieces are not equivalent to the two kilograms in Case 40.

The reported day and a half on site supports additional technician time under §7.1.7(g), provided the hours are distinct from line 9 under §7.1.8(c). Allow about 5.25 additional hours at €91 gross, or €478.
Section 7.1.7(f) limits this contractor to one travel charge on the invoice, even if a return visit was necessary for the same repair. The positive figure is nominal only.
Contractor protective equipment is excluded by §7.1.8(b), and no eligible consumable is separately priced. The positive figure is nominal only.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of the cut-out pipe and removed insulation. Allow €58 gross for the small load, consistent with Case 40.

Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.8(a) allow necessary removal of leak residues, but the combined line adds an undocumented coating and does not separate the eligible work. If itemised, allow about €100 gross for local cleaning and disinfection only, consistent with Case 36.
